seo.title: How to Check if ChatGPT Mentions Your Brand
seo.meta_description: How to check if ChatGPT mentions your brand: build a question set, test with and without search, record mentions and citations, and track changes monthly.

h1: How to Check if ChatGPT Mentions Your Brand (and Track It Monthly)
answer: To check if ChatGPT mentions your brand, list 20 to 50 questions your buyers actually ask, run each one in ChatGPT with web search on and off, and record whether you are named, how you are described and which pages are cited. Repeat the same set monthly, and watch chatgpt.com referrals in analytics to confirm the trend.
key_takeaways: Use real buyer questions, not your brand name alone.
Test with web search on and off; the answers differ.
Record mentions, descriptions, position and cited pages.
Answers vary between runs, so track trends, not single answers.
Confirm with chatgpt.com referral visits in analytics.

sections.heading: Why asking ChatGPT about your brand is not enough
sections.body_html: Typing your own company name into ChatGPT tells you whether it knows you exist, not whether it recommends you. Buyers rarely ask about you by name early on. They ask about their problem or their options: "which agencies help with AI search?", "best tent rental for a wedding in California". The real test is whether you appear in those answers.

sections.heading: Step 1: Build your question set
sections.body_html:
1. Collect questions from sales calls, support emails, reviews and your search data.
  2. Group them by stage: problem, solution, comparison and decision.
  3. Phrase them naturally, the way a buyer would type or speak them.
  4. Include location or industry where buyers would, such as "in Orange County" or "for e-commerce".
  5. Keep the list fixed so month-to-month results are comparable.

sections.heading: Step 2: Run the tests properly
sections.body_html:
• Use a clean session with memory and personalization off, or a fresh account, so past chats do not bias results.
  • Test with web search on to see which pages ChatGPT cites today.
  • Test without search to see what ChatGPT says from what it already knows.
  • Run important questions more than once, because answers vary.
  • Save the full answer, not just a yes or no.

sections.heading: Step 3: Record what matters
sections.body_html:
FieldWhat to note
Mentioned?Yes or no, and the position in the list
DescriptionHow ChatGPT describes your specialty and location
Cited pagesWhich of your URLs, if any, are linked
CompetitorsWho else is named, and in what order
AccuracyAnything wrong or outdated about you

A simple spreadsheet works. After a few months it shows clear patterns.

sections.heading: Step 4: Confirm with real traffic
sections.body_html: Tests show what ChatGPT says; analytics shows what it does for your business. Visits from ChatGPT usually arrive with chatgpt.com as the referrer, often tagged utm_source=chatgpt.com. Track those sessions by landing page, and connect them to form submissions so you can see leads, not just visits.

sections.heading: What to do with the results
sections.body_html:
• Not mentioned anywhere: check crawl access for OAI-SearchBot and publish pages that answer the missing questions directly.
  • Mentioned but described wrongly: fix the description on your site and profiles so it is consistent everywhere.
  • Mentioned, never cited: strengthen the matching page with a direct answer, specifics and sources.
  • Competitors always first: study the pages and sites cited for them and close the gaps.

sections.heading: A sample question set to copy
sections.body_html:
Here is a starting set for a GEO agency, to show the shape. Swap in your own category, audience and location:

  1. What is generative engine optimization?
  2. How do I get my brand recommended by ChatGPT?
  3. Best GEO agencies for e-commerce brands
  4. GEO agency in Orange County
  5. GEO vs SEO: which do I need?
  6. How much does a GEO audit cost?
  7. How long does GEO take to work?
  8. Which agencies help brands show up in Google AI Overviews?

Notice the mix: definitions, how-to questions, comparisons, local searches and price questions. Each stage of the buying journey needs at least a few questions, or you will miss where you are winning or losing.

sections.heading: How to read the results
sections.body_html:
After two or three monthly runs, look for patterns rather than single wins:

  • Mention rate: the share of questions where you are named. This is your headline number.
  • Citation rate: the share where one of your pages is linked. Citations send visits; mentions build awareness.
  • Average position: whether you appear first, in the middle or last when several brands are named.
  • Description accuracy: whether ChatGPT gets your specialty, location and strengths right.
  • Share by stage: many brands appear for definitions but vanish for comparison and decision questions, the ones closest to revenue.

Write each number down monthly. A small, steady rise across many questions is a much stronger signal than one dramatic answer.

sections.heading: How often to check, and who should own it
sections.body_html:
Monthly is the right rhythm for most businesses. AI answers shift as engines update their models and indexes, but week-to-week noise can hide the real trend. A monthly run of the same question set, done by the same person in the same way, produces numbers you can trust.

  • Owner: whoever runs marketing or SEO, so findings turn into page changes quickly.
  • Time needed: about two hours a month for a 30-question set across ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini.
  • Where to share it: a one-page summary with mention rate, citation rate and the three biggest gaps.

Run an extra check after any major change, such as a site redesign, a new service launch or a change to your robots.txt, so you can see its effect.

sections.heading: Checking other AI engines
sections.body_html: Use the same question set in Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot and Google AI Overviews. Perplexity is the easiest to study because every answer lists its sources. Comparing engines shows whether a gap is specific to one platform or a general problem with your pages or reputation.

faqs.q: How do I check if ChatGPT mentions my brand?
faqs.a: Build a list of 20 to 50 real buyer questions, run them in a clean ChatGPT session with web search on and off, and record whether you are mentioned, how you are described and which pages are cited. Repeat monthly with the same list.

faqs.q: Why does ChatGPT give different answers each time?
faqs.a: AI models generate answers fresh each time and may search different sources. That is why you should run important questions more than once and judge progress across many questions.

faqs.q: Should I turn off memory when testing ChatGPT?
faqs.a: Yes. Memory and past conversations can bias answers toward brands you have discussed. Use a clean session or temporary chat for consistent tests.

faqs.q: Can I see if ChatGPT sends me visitors?
faqs.a: Yes. Visits from ChatGPT usually show chatgpt.com as the referrer in Google Analytics, often with utm_source=chatgpt.com. Track them by landing page and tie them to leads.

faqs.q: What if ChatGPT says something wrong about my business?
faqs.a: Correct the information on your website, About page, profiles and directories so it is consistent everywhere. Over time, consistent and accurate sources improve what AI engines say.

faqs.q: Are there tools that track ChatGPT mentions?
faqs.a: Yes, several tools now track AI answers automatically. A spreadsheet with a fixed question set works well to start and helps you understand what to look for.
